_comment: Phase 18D: small, flat-chance positive events — deliberately simpler than data/events.json (no exposure/mitigation modeling). Rolled once per player per year (src/engine/events/positiveEvents.ts). Rewards are flat regardless of realm size by design: this is flavor, not a strategy lever, so it stays small relative to a mature economy while still meaning something early. "some funny ones as well" per the playtest request that asked for this.

A traveling salesman insists your castle needs a slightly bigger flag. You decline; he tips out of embarrassment.
Someone finally pays back the Baron who ruled three reigns ago. You were not expecting this.
A rival's messenger delivers a bribe to the wrong address. Yours.
A traveling dentist sets up shop, does brisk business, and leaves a "thank you" donation.
Your court jester wins a bet with a visiting noble. He shares the winnings, mostly.
A merchant caravan mistakes your border for a toll road that stopped existing decades ago. They pay anyway.
An anonymous benefactor leaves a sack of coin at the gate with a note reading simply "well governed."
A traveling astrologer predicts your prosperity, and several nobles pay handsomely to hear it confirmed.
Your scribes discover a clerical error that has been quietly costing the Kaiser money and not you.
A duel over a card game ends peacefully, and the loser insists on paying your treasury instead of his opponent.
A famous chef relocates to your lands purely for the produce. His apprentices follow within the year.
A traveling theater troupe likes it here so much they simply never leave.
Twins are born in the same week to three different families. Word travels; more families arrive hoping for luck.
A minor prophecy names your principality "a good place to raise children." People take it seriously.
A beekeeper's spectacular honey harvest becomes regional gossip, and with it, your reputation.
An old hermit comes down from the hills, likes what he sees, and tells everyone he knows. He knows a lot of people.
A visiting friar blesses the harvest. The harvest, coincidentally or not, turns out slightly better than expected.
A miller's scale was broken for months, undercounting deliveries. It is fixed, and the barns are fuller than the books claimed.
A rival principality's granary roof collapses. They sell the contents cheap rather than let it spoil, and you buy in.
A field thought exhausted produces one unexpectedly generous crop before finally giving out.
A traveling comedian performs in the square and the whole town is still laughing about it a week later.
A pig escapes the market and leads half the town on a chase. Nobody catches it, but everyone has a good story now.
Two feuding families settle their dispute over ale instead of at the gallows, to general relief.
A local legend turns out to be true, or at least everyone agrees to believe it is. Morale improves regardless.
The tavern keeper announces a "harvest special" and, for one evening, nobody complains about anything.
A traveling bard writes a song about your realm. It is not entirely accurate, but it is very catchy.
A stray dog adopts the guardhouse. Morale among the guards — and by extension everyone else — noticeably improves.
A minor miracle is reported at the local chapel. Investigation is inconclusive; enthusiasm is not.
The weather clears just in time for a long-planned market day, and everyone remembers it fondly for months.
A visiting acrobat troupe puts on an unscheduled show in the square. Even the tax collector stops to watch.
